Set up Farside

  1. Put the helper on your Mac. Download Farside for Mac from this website (coming soon), open it, and move it to Applications if it asks. It lives in the menu bar. You need macOS 26 or later on a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later).
  2. Allow two permissions. Screen Recording, so your iPhone can see the screen, and Accessibility, so taps become clicks and typing becomes typing. Farside opens the right settings page; flip the switch and the setup window notices by itself. macOS may ask you to quit and reopen Farside once.
  3. Get the app on your iPhone or iPad. Get Farside from the App Store (coming soon). You need iOS 26 or later or iPadOS 26 or later.
  4. Pair. On the Mac, choose Pair a Phone… in the Farside menu. In the app, tap Scan and point the camera at the code. Then choose Allow on the Mac. No account, no password.
  5. Allow Local Network on the phone. When iOS asks to find devices on your local network, choose Allow. That’s how your phone finds your Mac at home.
  6. Tap Connect. Your Mac appears. The first time, a short practice pad shows you how to steer; nothing you do there reaches the Mac.

The illustrated setup guide walks through the same steps with pictures.

How to steer

Your finger doesn’t go to the button: the pointer is already on it, and a tap anywhere clicks right there. More in using your iPhone as a Mac trackpad.

Farside gestures and what they do on the Mac
On your iPhoneOn your Mac
Slide one fingerMove the pointer (it moves, it doesn’t jump to your finger)
TapClick where the pointer is
Double-tapDouble-click
Two-finger tapRight-click
Two-finger dragScroll, up and down or sideways
Double-tap, hold, then slideDrag something
PinchZoom the view in or out; it follows your pointer
Three-finger swipeMission Control and switching Spaces
Swipe up on the handleShow the controls: keys, mic, clipboard, fit and mode
Double-tap the handleOpen the keyboard

Force Touch and pressure gestures can’t be done from a phone screen; use right-click or the app’s own buttons instead.

Can’t connect?

  1. Is the Mac awake and logged in? Farside can’t wake a sleeping Mac or get past the login screen.
  2. Is the Farside icon in the Mac’s menu bar, with sharing on?
  3. Are your phone and Mac on the same network? Or, away from home, is Anywhere active?
  4. Is Local Network allowed for Farside on the phone? Check Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network.
  5. Still stuck? Quit Farside on the Mac, open it again, and reconnect. Then write to us.

The Mac says permissions are missing

If you flipped the switch but Farside still says it can’t see or control the Mac, macOS may be holding on to an old permission.

  1. Quit Farside from its menu bar, open it again and check the setup window.
  2. Still not detected? Open System Settings › Privacy & Security, find Farside under Screen & System Audio Recording (or Accessibility), select it and remove it with the − button.
  3. Add it back with +, choosing Farside in Applications, and turn it on.
  4. Reopen Farside. The setup window updates by itself.

macOS sometimes asks again, every so often, whether Farside may keep recording the screen. Say yes on the Mac and sharing picks up where it left off.

What a message means

Every message in Farside says what happened and what to do. Here they all are, in case one needs more room.

Couldn’t reach your Mac.+

Your Mac may be asleep or offline, or Farside isn’t running on it.

Fix: Wake the Mac, check that the Farside icon is in its menu bar, then tap Try Again.

Your Mac isn’t available right now.+

The Mac isn’t sharing at the moment.

Fix: Check that it’s awake and logged in, and that Farside is in its menu bar with sharing on.

Your Mac is napping.+

It dozed off, so it can’t hear your phone.

Fix: Tap any key on the Mac or open its lid, then try again. To nap less, turn on Wake for network access in the Mac’s Battery or Energy settings.

Farside is still closing your last session.+

The previous connection hasn’t finished shutting down.

Fix: Wait a few seconds and try again.

Couldn’t verify this Mac.+

The secure handshake between your devices didn’t complete.

Fix: Try again. If it keeps happening, pair the phone again from the Farside menu on your Mac.

The connection glitched, so Farside ended the session to keep your Mac safe.+

Something arrived that didn’t look right, so Farside stopped instead of guessing.

Fix: Reconnect. Nothing on your Mac was changed by the glitch.

Reconnecting… (2 of 5)+

The network blinked. Farside is retrying by itself and keeps your zoom and position.

Fix: Give it a moment, or tap Cancel to stop trying.

You left Farside, so your Mac’s screen is hidden.+

Your Mac’s screen is covered whenever Farside isn’t on screen, so it can’t be seen in the app switcher.

Fix: Come back to Farside; it reconnects without pairing again if you return within a few minutes.

Waiting for your Mac’s screen…+

The connection is up and the first picture is on its way.

Fix: Give it a second. If it doesn’t arrive, end the session and connect again.

Your Mac stopped sharing its screen.+

macOS may be asking to renew Screen Recording permission, or someone chose Stop Sharing on the Mac.

Fix: On the Mac, open Farside from the menu bar and allow Screen Recording if macOS asks.

Reconnecting the picture. Controls are paused.+

The picture dropped for a moment, so taps are held back rather than sent blind.

Fix: Wait a moment; controls come back with the picture.

Mouse and keyboard are off on your Mac.+

You can see the Mac but not steer it: control is turned off, or Accessibility access is missing.

Fix: On the Mac, turn on Allow control in the Farside menu and check Farside is allowed under Privacy & Security › Accessibility.

Update Farside on your Mac to change picture quality.+

Your phone is newer than the Mac helper.

Fix: Choose Check for Updates… in the Farside menu on your Mac.

That’s too long to send at once.+

There’s a size limit on each piece of text you send or dictate.

Fix: Send it in two parts.

That code has expired.+

Pairing codes only last about two minutes, for safety.

Fix: On your Mac, choose New Code, then scan again.

That isn’t a Farside code.+

The camera found a QR code, just not ours.

Fix: Scan the code shown in Farside’s pairing window on your Mac.

Nobody approved this iPhone on the Mac in time.+

Pairing needs a yes on the Mac, and it waited about a minute.

Fix: Try again and choose Allow on the Mac when it asks.

Your Mac isn’t on this network.+

Free use works when your phone and Mac share a network. Reaching it over the internet needs the Anywhere plan.

Fix: Join the same Wi-Fi as your Mac, or try Anywhere free for 7 days.

Anywhere and billing

  • Try it: Anywhere starts with a 7-day free trial, then CA$5.99 a month or CA$49.99 a year (planned pricing, Canadian dollars).
  • Cancel or change plan: Settings › your name › Subscriptions on your iPhone or iPad. Cancel at least 24 hours before the renewal date to avoid the next charge.
  • Refunds: Apple handles them. Request one at reportaproblem.apple.com.
  • New phone? Use Restore Purchases in the app’s settings.
  • This website never asks for payment details.
